faq.q: What is the origin of Jaleh?
faq.a: Jaleh is associated with Persian. Jaleh is Persian ژاله (Zhāleh), meaning 'dew, hail'. It is used as a female given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Jaleh can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Jaleh should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zhāleh is a Persian word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.a: In Persian, Jaleh is rendered ژاله and carries the sense ژاله، شبنم.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Jaleh, jaleh. Script forms are ژاله, ژالہ, ژَالِه, ज़ाले.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
